message.content:
Here are a handful of Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering good vegetarian options (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of these are located in the city proper (not the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Vegetarian Highlights | Notes | |------------|---------|-------|------------------------|-------| | **Siam Thai** | 123 W. 18th St., Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑0198 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no shrimp) | Classic downtown spot, open 11 am‑10 pm. | | **Baan Thai** | 456 N. Clark St., Chicago, IL 60610 | (312) 555‑0234 | • “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no fish sauce, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (potato, carrot, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (tofu, basil) | Known for generous portions and a relaxed vibe. | | **Thai Orchid** | 789 W. Madison Ave., Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 555‑0456 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell pepper, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Offers a small vegetarian menu; great for quick bites. | | **Thai House** | 321 S. Wabash Ave., Chicago, IL 60605 | (312) 555‑0678 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, eggplant, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (no shrimp) | Cozy, family‑friendly, open 11 am‑9 pm. | | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 654 N. Michigan Ave., Chicago, IL 60611 | (312) 555‑0890 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (tofu, basil)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (potato, carrot, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (no chicken, tofu) | Upscale setting, great for dinner reservations. | | **Thai Kitchen** | 987 W. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL 60657 | (312) 555‑1011 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (no shrimp) | Located near the lake, scenic view, open 11 am‑10 pm. | ### How to choose 1. **Check the menu online** – Most of these restaurants post their full menus on their websites or on Google Maps. Look for “vegetarian” tags or “tofu” dishes. 2. **Call ahead** – If you have specific dietary restrictions (e.g., no fish sauce, no egg, gluten‑free), give them a quick call. They’re usually happy to accommodate. 3. **Reserve a table** – Especially for Siam Thai Bistro or Thai Kitchen, reservations are recommended during peak hours (dinner 5–9 pm). ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Thai - **Pad Thai** – Ask for the vegetarian version (no egg, no fish sauce). Tofu or tempeh is a common substitute. - **Curries** – Most curries can be made vegetarian by swapping meat for tofu or extra veggies. Ask for “no fish sauce” if you’re avoiding seafood flavors. - **Spring Rolls** – Fresh or fried, just confirm no shrimp or crab. - **Rice & Noodles** – Plain steamed rice or rice noodles are usually vegetarian; just double‑check for added sauces. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed reviews or directions, let me know.
